# Justice Community Overdose Innovation Network Coordination and Translation Center (JCOIN CTC)

> > JCOIN CTC coordinates research and translation to address the opioid crisis among justice-involved populations through medication-assisted treatment, peer recovery support, and implementation science.

The Justice Community Overdose Innovation Network Coordination and Translation Center (JCOIN CTC) is funded by NIDA/NIH to advance evidence-based interventions for opioid use disorder in criminal justice settings. The center supports research hubs, rapid innovation grants (J-RIG), and translational activities focused on MOUD/MAT implementation, problem-solving courts, corrections-based treatment, and overdose prevention strategies.

## Key Topics

- Opioid Use Disorder (OUD)
- Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD/MAT)
- Justice-involved populations
- Criminal justice research
- Problem-solving courts and drug courts
- Peer recovery support services
- Overdose prevention
- Implementation science
- JCOIN research network
- Corrections-based treatment
- Methadone and naltrexone
- Opioid hackathons
- Health disparities and spatial inequities
- Veterans Treatment Courts
- Community-based participatory research (CBPR)

## Research on MOUD/MAT Implementation

- [Fostering MOUD use in justice populations: Assessing the comparative effectiveness of two favored implementation strategies to increase MOUD use](https://www.jcoinctc.org/fostering-moud-use-in-justice-populations-assessing-the-comparative-effectiveness-of-two-favored-implementation-strategies-to-increase-moud-use): Todd Molfenter protocol comparing NIATx vs ECHO for MOUD implementation
- ["Yeah, this is not going to work for me"-The impact of federal policy restrictions on methadone continuation upon release from jail or prison](https://www.jcoinctc.org/yeah-this-is-not-going-to-work-for-me-the-impact-of-federal-policy-restrictions-on-methadone-continuation-upon-release-from-jail-or-prison): Justin Berk study on federal methadone policy barriers post-release
- [Maintenance on extended-release naltrexone is associated with reduced injection opioid use among justice-involved persons with opioid use disorder](https://www.jcoinctc.org/maintenance-on-extended-release-naltrexone-is-associated-with-reduced-injection-opioid-use-among-justice-involved-persons-with-opioid-use-disorder): Audun Lier study on extended-release naltrexone reducing injection use
- [New Aced It Episode: The Benefits and Implementation Challenges of the First State-Wide Comprehensive Medication for Addictions Program in a Unified Jail and Prison Setting](https://www.jcoinctc.org/aced-it-the-benefits-and-implementation-challenges): Aced It podcast S2E6 on statewide jail/prison MAT program challenges

## Criminal Justice Settings and Problem-Solving Courts

- [Access Differential: Comparing Problem-solving Courts and Probation](https://www.jcoinctc.org/access-differential-comparing-problem-solving-courts-and-probation): Lindsay Smith research on MAT access in drug courts vs probation
- [Recommendations to Improve the Service Quality in Veteran Treatment Courts](https://www.jcoinctc.org/recommendations-to-improve-the-service-quality-in-veteran-treatment-courts): Kim Kras qualitative research on Veterans Treatment Courts quality
- [Evidence‑based Treatment for SUD in CMHCs: The ACCESS Program](https://www.jcoinctc.org/evidence%e2%80%91based-treatment-for-sud-in-cmhcs-the-access-program): Matt Aalsma's ACCESS Program for SUD treatment in community mental health

## Peer Recovery Support and Community Services

- [Peer Recovery Support Services Across the Continuum: In Community, Hospital, Corrections, and Treatment and Recovery Agency Settings - A Narrative Review](https://www.jcoinctc.org/peer-recovery-support-services-across-the-continuum-in-community-hospital-corrections-and-treatment-and-recovery-agency-settings-a-narrative-review): Narrative review of peer recovery support across corrections settings
- [Ending the HIV Epidemic for Persons Who Use Drugs: The Practical Challenges of Meeting People Where They Are](https://www.jcoinctc.org/ending-the-hiv-epidemic-for-persons-who-use-drugs-the-practical-challenges-of-meeting-people-where-they-are): Challenges in EHE implementation for persons using drugs with PrEP
- [Maltreatment, resilience, and sexual relationship power in a sample of justice-involved women with opioid use disorder](https://www.jcoinctc.org/maltreatment-resilience-and-sexual-relationship-power-in-a-sample-of-justice-involved-women-with-opioid-use-disorder): Jaxin Annett study on trauma and relationship power in women with OUD

## JCOIN Research Studies and Initiatives

- [JCOIN Rapid Innovation Grant (J-RIG) Program](https://www.jcoinctc.org/000-j-rig): J-RIG program funding rapid innovation for justice-involved OUD research
- [Opioid Hackathon as Implementation Strategy (013)](https://www.jcoinctc.org/opioid-hackathon-as-implementation-strategy-013): Study 013: Hackathon feasibility for opioid visualization tools
- [Social/Spatial Inequities and OUD/HCV Outcomes (019)](https://www.jcoinctc.org/social-spatial-inequities-and-oud-hcv-outcomes-019): Study 019: Agent-based modeling of OUD/HCV spatial health disparities

## Innovation and Public Engagement

- [2 Days, Countless Lives Saved - Hackathon Winners Develop Viable Solutions to Combat Opioid Addiction](https://www.jcoinctc.org/2-days-countless-lives-saved): UCIPT Opioid Hackathon winners develop iPill and ML solutions
- [Feasibility of a citizen-driven hackathon to increase public engagement and solutions to address the opioid crisis](https://www.jcoinctc.org/feasibility-of-a-citizen-driven-hackathon-to-increase-public-engagement-and-solutions-to-address-opioid-crisis): Stephanie Soliz study on citizen hackathon for opioid crisis solutions
- [JCOIN Webinar: Xylazine Prevalence and Response Strategies](https://www.jcoinctc.org/jcoin-webinar-xylazine-prevalence-and-response-strategies): JCOIN/NIDA webinar on xylazine prevalence and response strategies
